title: people-ops-self-notes-manager-prep-q1-2026
content:
Manager prep + self-notes (Q1 2026) - Jamal Harris

Context / purpose:
- Quick scratchpad for my upcoming 1:1 with Lena (week of Mar 8).
- Draft of self-review highlights and areas I want support on.
- List of proposed goals and suggested metrics for the next quarter.

Top wins (since last review):
1) Ops playbook for new hiring panel workflows
   - Reduced panel scheduling time by ~25% (tracked in HireFlow logs, ticket HR-3187).
   - Created standardized rubric template; being piloted with Backend hiring team.
2) Manager enablement series (pilot run for eng managers)
   - Designed 4-session curriculum, ran two pilots with 10 managers each.
   - Feedback: average 4.2/5 usefulness. Requesting budget to scale (see linked Confluence doc).
3) Onboarding checklist revamp for Private deployment team
   - Cut time-to-first-commit for new hires by estimated 1 week (anecdotal; need more data).

Areas to own / propose as goals (Q2 planning):
- Goal A: Scale manager enablement program to 40 managers by EOW Q2.
  - Success metrics: number of managers trained (target 40), post-training NPS >= 4.0, 3 follow-up coaching sessions scheduled for each cohort.
- Goal B: Improve hiring pipeline predictability for infra roles
  - Success metrics: time-to-offer median <= 28 days for infra/serving-runtime roles; increase offer acceptance rate to >= 78%.
- Goal C: Launch internal career ladder workshops (ICL) for ICs
  - Success metrics: run 3 workshops, collect ladder calibration feedback, produce 1-pager for managers.

Self-review bullets (to copy into formal form):
- Strengths: organized execution (project plans, docs), stakeholder alignment across Eng/Product/SRE, strong facilitation skills for manager cohorts.
- Impact examples: see Wins above; also led cross-functional retro that surfaced 3 process changes adopted by Platform Eng.
- Development areas: need better quantitative measurement strategies (work with Data team to instrument hiring funnel), delegate more tactical onboarding tasks to coordinator.
- Feedback I received: "Really helpful facilitating sticky people conversations; more templates please" (from Product managers).

Asks for manager (what I want from Lena):
- Prioritization: help me decide whether to push hard on scaling manager enablement vs focusing on hiring pipeline fixes this quarter.
- Headcount/budget: can we allocate a 0.5 FTE contractor to help run scheduling and workshop ops (budget ask: ~$20k for Q2)?
- Mentorship: want to shadow Lena on executive stakeholder updates; request 2 sessions where I present a brief and get feedback.
- Promotion calibration: I think I'm ready to be considered for Senior People Ops (outline below). Would appreciate candid feedback and next steps.

Promotion case (draft outline):
- Role stretch: already owning cross-functional programs (manager enablement, onboarding, hiring playbooks) that impact org-wide health.
- Deliverables: documented playbooks, training curriculum, pilot outcomes with metrics.
- Leadership: consistent facilitator for manager forums; starting to coach new managers.
- Gaps: need clearer ownership of a measurable org-wide KPI and stronger partnership with data/ops for instrumentation.

Concrete next steps / 1:1 agenda:
1) Quick sync (5m): How are you? any urgent priorities?
2) Review wins & metrics (10m): highlight 2 biggest wins and numbers we can share upward.
3) Discuss Q2 goal prioritization (15m): pick top 1-2 goals and define success metrics.
4) Promotion conversation (10m): get Lena's view and actionable next steps.
5) Admin / asks (5m): budget for contractor, shadowing sessions, and any calendar prep.

Open questions / things to follow up on:
- Can Data prep a small dashboard for hiring funnel (time-to-offer, acceptance rate) by Apr 15? Who to loop in (Aisha?)
- Budget: is $20k realistic for a contractor this quarter? If no, prioritize which parts of scale do we cut.
- Measurement: how to better estimate time-saved for onboarding changes (do we track time-to-first-commit in GitHub?).

Notes to self (informal):
- Bring concrete anecdote about Julieta (new manager) who reported the rubric helped calibrate interviews.
- Prep the 1-pager for promotion with 3-4 bullet impact examples + ask for specific stretch assignments.
- Remove unnecessary jargon when presenting to execs; focus on business impact: hiring speed, manager retention, ramp time.

Draft email to Lena (send day before 1:1):
"Hi Lena — putting a quick agenda for tomorrow's 1:1. I want to review Q1 highlights, get your input on Q2 priorities (manager enablement vs hiring pipeline), and discuss potential promotion calibration. Also want to ask about a short budget request for a part-time contractor to help scale workshops. Attached: short win summary and proposed goals. — Jamal"

Last quick TODOs before meeting:
- Pull raw pilot feedback + NPS (Aisha said she'll share CSV)
- Draft 1-pager for promotion case (first pass by Mar 5)
- Confirm time with Lena and add agenda to calendar (done?).

-- end of notes --
